To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) circadian regulation of transcription is widespread in the mammalian genome, 2) circadian-regulated transcription is highly tissue-specific, 3) the circadian clock is a key determinant of tissue-specific gene expression, and 4) the circadian oscillator regulates transcription through a combination of tissue-specific and general transcription factors.
the circadian oscillator regulates transcription in nearly all tissues of the body and that this regulation is critical to the temporal coordination of physiological and behavioural processes.
the circadian clock regulates a large proportion of the transcriptome in both the SCN and liver and that the circadian output in the SCN differs from that in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of temporal gene expression in the mammalian circadian system.
the identification of circadian-regulation in the mouse, and the analysis of the molecular mechanisms underlying such regulation.
understanding how the circadian clock orchestrates transcription in the SCN and peripheral organs to coordinate daily physiology and behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
circadian oscillators regulate the expression of a large number of transcripts in most, if not all, organs and tissues.
the circadian clock regulates the majority of the genome in a tissue-specific manner.
circadian transcriptional output is widespread, tissue-specific and pervasive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the circadian system is an integral part of the transcriptional regulatory network of the cell, and the clock controls transcriptional output by acting on both the rate and the time of expression of key and rate-limitting steps in major cellular processes and pathways.
circadian transcriptional output is pervasive and tissue-specific.
the mammalian circadian system is capable of controlling the expression of a vast number of genes and that the circadian system is able to regulate a wide array of physiological processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
circadian regulation of transcription is a pervasive phenomenon, and that circadian regulation can be found in nearly every process that is important for the physiology and behaviour of an animal.
the circadian clock controls a large number of genes in the SCN and the liver.
circadian regulation of gene expression in the liver and the SCN is extensive.
